scope: Primary-source/report-chain evidence for three specified keys only. Original retrievals are not upgrades to the current replicating-source texts. No canonical records or audit classifications written.

coverage.shipped_comparator_reference: 1101; read only as supplied identity, no dataset edits

cohort_and_report_chain.answer: Original HMG introduction explicitly connects its earlier 65-family analysis (reference 44, AJHG 72:1053) to recruitment of 180 additional families. Its 362-family sample contains 85 strong-history families. This establishes overlapping expansion reports, not an independent new cohort inferred from year or DOI. Family-level inclusion lists were unavailable; exact retention of every earlier pedigree is not independently checked.
original_locations: HMG Introduction and Results: strong-history stratification

finding_identity.answer: Both reports contain the chromosome 2q36–37 susceptibility finding in strong-history multiplex PD families. The HMG paper additionally reports other loci and interaction analyses. Same locus and overlapping recruitment do not make the whole papers or every estimator equivalent. AJHG reports an autosomal-dominant multipoint peak of 5.1 at D2S206; HMG describes nonparametric genome scans and a 4.9 chromosome-2 signal in 85 strong-history families. Do not relabel that 4.9 as an identical autosomal-dominant estimate.

closest_finding_chain.answer: Prestel’s 45-family European study selects the D2S126–D2S125 interval, matches the strong-history rule and performs autosomal-dominant as well as nonparametric linkage analyses. Its 39.5-cM/5.1/D2S206 framing most specifically matches the AJHG strong-history finding; HMG is an explicit expanded-sample continuation and a direct discussion comparator. The design does not identify a separate retest of HMG’s new chromosome-10/14 interaction findings. Neither later date nor a singular reference to an original study decides the chain.

conditional_answers: If the target is strong-history PARK11 regional susceptibility, the evidence supports a common finding chain with overlapping expansion waves and both 2003 reports contributing published evidence.

If the target requires the specific HMG 85-family 4.9 estimator or its separate interaction findings, inspect the estimator and tested variables: Prestel does not reproduce the 85-family dataset and does not test those additional interaction claims.
limits: The 39.5-cM interval is verified in Prestel’s description; AJHG’s own summary describes a 20-cM region. These interval descriptions are not silently treated as identical support intervals.

Initial-sample descriptions differ by diagnostic filtering: Prestel mentions 160 families/170 pairs, whereas HMG describes a previous 182 families/203 pairs and distinguishes 194 verified families in the expanded analysis. Do not force these counts to denote identical inclusion sets.
HMG indexed text is available but publisher PDF bytes remain blocked. Figure-derived details are not used as literal evidence.

cohort_and_report_chain.answer: Olbrich explicitly reuses earlier patient/control EEG data and cites Hegerl as reference 6; its discussion again identifies the same study population. Thus reuse is supported by report text, independently of equal N. Its separate 141-person healthy clustering cohort does not establish a new 30/30 clinical cohort.
cohort_and_report_chain.reference_locator: Olbrich page 194, reference 6; pages 189 and 193 for reuse statements.

finding_identity.answer: Hegerl’s original author abstract distinguishes fractions of individual vigilance stages and latencies to first occurrence. It describes more A1, less A2/A3/B2/3, and later A2/A3/B2/3 in MDD. It is not merely a generic vigilance citation.
finding_identity.source_limit: Full Hegerl body unavailable; original findings are established from the complete preserved author abstract.

current_empirical_comparison.answer: Ip empirically compares MDD and healthy-control stage percentages as well as median vigilance and vigilance slopes. Fractions therefore receive a partial operational retest: A2/A3 are pooled, recording windows and analysis differ, and main-text methods describe no stage-onset latency test. The dynamic slope comparison addresses the broader hyperstability association. The available text does not establish a separate faithful retest of every Hegerl endpoint.

conditional_answers: If the target is the stage-fraction MDD/control finding, Ip supplies an actual empirical comparison, with pooled stages and shorter windows that must remain explicit.
If the target is Hegerl’s individual A2 and A3 fractions and stage-specific onset latencies, the inspected main text does not establish that full endpoint set.
Whether the common cohort supports one or multiple record entries is outside this evidence-only deliverable. Distinct published findings must be evaluated separately from cohort identity.
limits: Hegerl full body, detailed latency definition/censoring and complete original tables were not recovered.
Ip supplemental model tables were not recovered; no absolute claim is made about uninspected supplement contents.

cohort_and_report_chain.answer: The clinical comparison reuses the Hegerl EEG dataset; this is stated explicitly in Olbrich, not inferred from the matching 30/30 counts. The 141 healthy volunteers form a different clustering dataset.

finding_identity.answer: Olbrich adds K-means-derived vigilance patterns, selects a three-cluster solution using gap statistics, assigns independent clinical EEG time courses to nearest centroids, and tests diagnostic pattern frequencies. This is a separate published analytic finding despite clinical data reuse.
original_locations: Methods: Cluster Analysis and Comparison of EEG Vigilance Phenotypes
Results: Vigilance Phenotypes in Depressed Patients and HCs

current_empirical_comparison.answer: Ip states a case-control hyperstability aim and measures slopes, medians and stage fractions. Its inspected main-text methods do not apply the three published centroids, recreate K-means/gap selection, compare the three diagnostic cluster frequencies, or estimate sensitivity/specificity for that cluster classifier. Ip’s ROC analysis concerns clinical treatment-response discrimination, which does not establish a retest of Olbrich’s MDD/control cluster classifier.

conditional_answers: If the target is the broad stable-vigilance/MDD association, Ip tests related case-control behavior in an independent NeuroPharm sample.

If the target is the derived three-cluster diagnostic-pattern finding, the inspected main text does not establish its empirical retest. Citation and a shared general direction cannot substitute for that method comparison.
Shared clinical data do not erase the distinct cluster-derived publication; distinct paper identifiers also do not prove that Ip retested that distinct finding.
